title: Optimizing Multi-Stage Docker (<25MB) & Building Zero-Downtime CI/CD with GitHub Actions
summary: Ultralight container packaging on Alpine, Nginx SPA fallback routing, and automated static typechecks in delivery pipelines.
author: Tan Huynh Nhat

sections.article-objectives: Provide a comprehensive guide to building ultralight SPA container images (< 25MB) using Docker Multi-Stage builds on Alpine Linux, combined with an automated GitHub Actions CI/CD workflow to achieve seamless, zero-downtime production delivery.
sections.architecture-principles:
The containerization architecture decouples compilation from production serving:

  • Stage 1 (Build Environment): Uses node:20-alpine to install packages, run TypeScript typechecks, and compile static production bundles into /dist.
  • Stage 2 (Runtime Server): Copies only the compiled /dist artifacts into nginx:alpine-slim (< 15MB) with custom caching headers, gzip compression, and SPA fallback routing.
  • GitHub Actions CI/CD: Triggered on commits and PRs, automating Lint -> Test -> Build -> Docker Registry Push -> Zero-Downtime Server Reload.
sections.step-by-step-setup:
Implementation steps:

  • Step 1: Create a multi-stage Dockerfile with non-root execution and comprehensive .dockerignore rules.
  • Step 2: Configure nginx.conf with try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; and immutable caching policies for hashed assets.
  • Step 3: Author .github/workflows/deploy.yml leveraging GitHub Actions Cache and Docker Buildx to accelerate build times by 3x.
sections.troubleshooting-pitfalls:
• 404 errors on browser refresh: Missing SPA fallback routing in Nginx. Resolved by adding try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html.
  • Bloated Docker images: Caused by accidental bundling of node_modules or omitting the runtime copy stage.
  • Security vulnerabilities: Running containers as root. Always configure non-root users (USER nginx).
sections.evaluation-scaling: Reduced container image size from 850MB to 22MB and deployment latency from 6 minutes down to 45 seconds. Future roadmap: Incorporate Trivy vulnerability scanning into PR checks and establish Kubernetes Canary rollouts.
